name: Bathroom

photos.caption: The finished room: shower, WC, basin, pink ceiling and disco ball
JOB 1 — behind the toilet: waste connector exposed in a rough hole, pan not tight to the wall
JOB 2 — the row of glass blocks at the top of the wall above the door, to be tiled over
JOB 3 — door from the kitchen side: sliding door too short, surround unfinished, glass blocks above

current.summary: Small shower room, essentially finished: black-framed sliding shower enclosure on a dark tray with black thermostatic shower set, blush vertical tiles in the shower, large grey stone-effect tiles on the other walls and floor, back-to-wall WC with concealed cistern, small wall-hung basin with black tap, black shelving, Edison-bulb wall light, pink ceiling with disco ball, a gold testa di moro on the shelf. The door is an old white panelled door hung as a slider on a top track; it is too short for the opening. Three jobs remain.
keep: Everything else — shower, tiles, WC, basin, ceiling, disco ball
issues: JOB 1 — Behind the toilet: the waste connector shows through a rough hole in the tile and the pan stands off the wall
JOB 2 — Tile over the row of glass blocks at the top of the wall (bathroom side)
JOB 3 — Finish the door surround and fit a door of the right height: 210 cm

orientation: No window. A row of glass blocks at the top of the wall above the door borrows light from/to the kitchen (to be tiled over on the bathroom side)

target.concept: The room is done to your taste — pink ceiling, disco ball, black fittings, blush tiles. Target state is simply the three jobs finished cleanly: nothing showing behind the WC, a clean tiled band where the glass blocks were, and a full-height (210 cm) door in a properly finished surround.

palette.name: Dead Salmon
palette.role: ceiling (if repainting the pink in a softer tone)

materials.name: Basin shelf / mini vanity
materials.detail: Oak or local stone, hides the waste

lighting.name: IP44 wall light by the mirror

scope: Job 1: make good behind the WC so no pipe or hole is visible
Job 2: tile over the glass blocks on the bathroom side
Job 3: finish the door surround and supply/fit a sliding door 210 cm high

surfaces.prep: Pull the pan forward; check the waste connection is sound and sealed. Fit a shorter/straight pan connector so the pan sits tight to the wall; cut in a tile patch (same grey tile) or neat collar to close the rough hole.
surfaces.finish: Re-fix pan, silicone bead (white, sanitary) pan-to-wall and pan-to-floor
surfaces.notes: If no spare tile: a white or black pipe collar/rosette plus silicone is the fallback

surfaces.surface: Glass-block row above door, bathroom side (Job 2)
surfaces.prep: Glass is non-porous — tiles will not bond to it directly. Either (a) apply a grip primer for non-absorbent surfaces, or (b, more reliable) fix a thin tile-backer board over the blocks. Rake out and fill the mortar joints flush first.
surfaces.finish: Tile to the ceiling with flexible (S1) adhesive; grout to match
surfaces.colour: Grey stone-effect tile (existing) — or the blush vertical tile, to choose
surfaces.notes: Tiling over removes the borrowed daylight: the room will rely fully on artificial light and needs a working extractor fan

surfaces.prep: Square up and plaster the broken reveal and both faces round the opening; fit a timber or plaster lining and architraves each side; make good the wall above the track
surfaces.finish: Paint surround to match walls; door in warm white eggshell
surfaces.notes: New sliding door 210 cm high (Italian standard height — off-the-shelf leaves exist at 60/70/80 × 210). Width of the opening to be measured before ordering. Alternative: a carpenter lengthens the existing antique door with an added bottom rail so the old door and brass handles are kept.

notes: Do not disturb the shower enclosure, tray, tiles or fittings
Sliding door: the ornate projecting handles will stop the door sliding fully back — use flush pulls on a new door, or accept a part-open stop on the old one
Kitchen side of the glass blocks: confirm whether they stay visible or are plastered over
brief.access: Room in daily use — agree working days
